nodes.name: WebIDL.py
nodes.summary: Third-party WebIDL parser (Mozilla variant) that lexes and parses WebIDL source into an AST of IDL classes, validates it, and resolves identifiers and types. Serves as the backbone of Servo's script-bindings code generation.
nodes.languageNotes: Large single-file Python parser using a class hierarchy of ~60 AST node types, a hand-written Tokenizer, and a 172-method recursive-descent Parser.

nodes.name: WebIDLError
nodes.summary: WebIDL parse error type carrying a source location and message for syntax/semantic failures.

nodes.name: Location
nodes.summary: Source location (filename, line, column) within a WebIDL file being parsed.

nodes.name: BuiltinLocation
nodes.summary: Predefined location marker for built-in WebIDL objects not originating from user source text.

nodes.name: IDLObject
nodes.summary: Abstract base class for all WebIDL AST nodes, providing common validation and naming utilities.

nodes.name: IDLScope
nodes.summary: Named scope holding a set of IDL objects; supports name lookups, redefinition checks, and exports.

nodes.name: IDLIdentifier
nodes.summary: A named WebIDL identifier carrying an optional location.

nodes.name: IDLUnresolvedIdentifier
nodes.summary: Identifier that references a definition not yet resolved, resolved later against a scope.

nodes.name: IDLObjectWithIdentifier
nodes.summary: Mixin adding identifier handling to an IDL object.

nodes.name: IDLObjectWithScope
nodes.summary: Mixin adding scope handling to an IDL object.

nodes.name: IDLIdentifierPlaceholder
nodes.summary: Placeholder identifier used to stand in for forward references before resolution.

nodes.name: IDLExposureMixins
nodes.summary: Mixins implementing the [Exposed] extended attribute and global-name exposure logic.

nodes.name: IDLExternalInterface
nodes.summary: Reference to an interface defined outside of the WebIDL being parsed (e.g. an external API surface).

nodes.name: IDLPartialDictionary
nodes.summary: A partial dictionary definition that extends an existing dictionary.

nodes.name: IDLPartialInterfaceOrNamespace
nodes.summary: A partial interface or namespace definition that extends an existing one.

nodes.name: IDLOperations
nodes.summary: Container holding a set of named operations (methods) for an interface-like definition.

nodes.name: IDLInterfaceOrInterfaceMixinOrNamespace
nodes.summary: Common base for interface, interface-mixin, and namespace definitions sharing member handling.

nodes.name: IDLInterfaceMixin
nodes.summary: An interface mixin definition whose members may be mixed into other interfaces.

nodes.name: ReflectedHTMLAttributesReturningFrozenArray
nodes.summary: Helper that reflects HTML attributes and produces frozen array return types for generated bindings.

nodes.name: IDLInterfaceOrNamespace
nodes.summary: Common base for interface and namespace definitions.

nodes.name: IDLInterface
nodes.summary: A WebIDL interface definition, the central AST node representing an object type with members.

nodes.name: IDLNamespace
nodes.summary: A WebIDL namespace definition grouping related constants, attributes, and operations.

nodes.name: IDLDictionary
nodes.summary: A WebIDL dictionary definition, a keyed collection of optional members.

nodes.name: IDLEnum
nodes.summary: A WebIDL enum definition listing a set of allowed string values.

nodes.name: IDLType
nodes.summary: Abstract base class for all WebIDL type representations, with type-flattening and coercion helpers.

nodes.name: IDLUnresolvedType
nodes.summary: A type reference that has not yet been resolved to a concrete type definition.

nodes.name: IDLParametrizedType
nodes.summary: A parametrized type (e.g. Foo<T>) wrapping a type parameter.

nodes.name: IDLNullableType
nodes.summary: A nullable type (T?) wrapping an underlying non-nullable type.

nodes.name: IDLSequenceType
nodes.summary: The sequence<T> type representing an ordered list of a single element type.

nodes.name: IDLRecordType
nodes.summary: The record<K,V> type mapping string keys to values.

nodes.name: IDLObservableArrayType
nodes.summary: An observable array type whose mutations are observable by script bindings.

nodes.name: IDLUnionType
nodes.summary: A union type representing a value that may be one of several member types.

nodes.name: IDLTypedefType
nodes.summary: A type reference to a named typedef, resolving to its underlying type.

nodes.name: IDLTypedef
nodes.summary: A typedef definition giving a name to an underlying WebIDL type.

nodes.name: IDLWrapperType
nodes.summary: A type wrapping a callback interface, representing the callback object type.

nodes.name: IDLPromiseType
nodes.summary: The promise<T> type representing an asynchronous result value.

nodes.name: IDLBuiltinType
nodes.summary: A built-in primitive WebIDL type (e.g. long, double, DOMString) with coercion rules.

nodes.name: NoCoercionFoundError
nodes.summary: Error raised when no valid coercion exists between two WebIDL types.

nodes.name: IDLValue

nodes.name: IDLNullValue

nodes.name: abortcontroller.rs
nodes.summary: Implements the Web AbortController DOM interface, providing an object that can signal an associated AbortSignal to cancel operations.

nodes.name: AbortController
nodes.summary: DOM interface holding an associated AbortSignal and exposing Abort/Signal operations per the AbortController WebIDL.

nodes.name: new_with_proto
nodes.summary: Constructs an AbortController with a given prototype and a freshly created AbortSignal.

nodes.name: signal_abort
nodes.summary: Signals the associated AbortSignal with a reason, triggering abort algorithms.

nodes.name: abortsignal.rs
nodes.summary: Implements the AbortSignal DOM interface including dependent signals, abort algorithms, and the static Abort/Timeout/Any factories.
nodes.languageNotes: Tracks dependent signals and abort algorithms with weak references for garbage collection.

nodes.name: AbortSignal
nodes.summary: EventTarget-derived DOM interface that carries an abort reason and runs registered abort algorithms when signaled.

nodes.name: signal_abort
nodes.summary: Fires the abort algorithms with a reason, sets the abort flag, and dispatches the abort event.

nodes.name: run_abort_algorithm
nodes.summary: Executes a single registered abort algorithm variant (event listener, fetch, stream piping, etc.).

nodes.name: create_dependent_abort_signal
nodes.summary: Creates a dependent AbortSignal that aborts when any of the given source signals aborts, used by AbortSignal.any().

nodes.name: Abort
nodes.summary: Static AbortSignal.abort() that returns an already-aborted signal with the provided reason.

nodes.name: Timeout
nodes.summary: Static AbortSignal.timeout() that aborts a signal after the given number of milliseconds via a timer task.

nodes.name: Any
nodes.summary: Static AbortSignal.any() that creates a dependent signal aborting when any input signal aborts.

nodes.name: mod.rs
nodes.summary: Module barrel re-exporting the abort-related DOM interfaces (AbortController and AbortSignal).

nodes.name: activation.rs
nodes.summary: Defines the Activatable trait implementing DOM activation behavior for elements that can be activated (e.g., via click).

nodes.name: Activatable
nodes.summary: Trait providing activation and legacy pre-activation behavior hooks shared by activatable DOM elements.

nodes.name: animation.rs
nodes.summary: Implements the Web Animations Animation interface, tying an animation to a timeline and an associated effect.

nodes.name: Animation
nodes.summary: EventTarget-derived interface holding a timeline and an associated animation effect with play-state management.

nodes.name: animationeffect.rs
nodes.summary: Implements the AnimationEffect interface and timing-property parsing shared by keyframe effects.

nodes.name: AnimationEffect
nodes.summary: Base interface for animation effects, holding specified timing properties and computing resolved timing values.

nodes.name: update_the_timing_properties
nodes.summary: Parses and validates an EffectTiming dictionary, updating the effect's specified timing properties.

nodes.name: animationtimeline.rs
nodes.summary: Implements the base AnimationTimeline interface providing a current time value for animations.

nodes.name: AnimationTimeline
nodes.summary: Base timeline interface exposing and advancing a current time used to drive animations.

nodes.name: documenttimeline.rs

nodes.summary: Wrapper around kurbo's BezPath exposing canvas drawing commands (move_to, line_to, curves, arc, ellipse, rect) and hit-testing.

nodes.name: CanvasCommand
nodes.summary: Large enum enumerating all commands sent to the paint thread for 2D canvas operations such as drawing images, filling/stroking paths, text, and pixel data.

nodes.name: FillOrStrokeStyle
nodes.summary: Enum of paint styles for fill/stroke: solid color, linear gradient, radial gradient, or a surface pattern.

nodes.name: LinearGradientStyle
nodes.summary: Struct describing a linear gradient defined by two points and a list of color stops.

nodes.name: RadialGradientStyle
nodes.summary: Struct describing a radial gradient defined by two circles and a list of color stops.

nodes.name: SurfaceStyle
nodes.summary: Struct describing a surface pattern with repeat and transform options for fill/stroke.

nodes.name: CompositionOrBlending
nodes.summary: Enum combining composition and blending operations, with string parsing to map CSS-like keywords to the appropriate style.

nodes.name: CanvasFont
nodes.summary: Represents a canvas font, resolving to font data and an index, either cached locally or through a local font identifier.

nodes.name: TextRun
nodes.summary: A laid-out text run carrying font, point size, glyph positions, advance and bounds.

nodes.name: arc_to
nodes.summary: Implements the HTML canvas arcTo algorithm, computing tangent points and drawing a circular arc between two points.

nodes.name: ellipse
nodes.summary: Builds an elliptical arc path by decomposing the ellipse into kurbo Arc segments across the requested angle sweep.

nodes.name: bezier_curve_to
nodes.summary: Appends a cubic Bezier curve to the path after validating all control points are finite.

nodes.name: rect
nodes.summary: Adds a rectangular sub-path built from four line segments plus a closing move.

nodes.name: is_point_in_path
nodes.summary: Determines whether a point lies within the path using winding or segment distance tests according to the fill rule.

nodes.name: lib.rs
nodes.summary: Crate root for the shared canvas module that declares the canvas and webgl submodules and the ConstellationCanvasMsg enum for cross-process canvas lifecycle messages.

nodes.name: ConstellationCanvasMsg
nodes.summary: Enum of messages exchanged with the constellation for canvas lifecycle: creation, memory reporting, and exit.

nodes.name: webgl.rs
nodes.summary: Defines the shared WebGL infrastructure: the WebGLCommand enum mirroring the GL API, WebGL/WebXR message types, thread/channel plumbing, context results, error enums, GL limits, and sized-data-type introspection.
nodes.languageNotes: WebGLCommand enumerates hundreds of GL entry points, and SizedDataType maps GL enum constants to their component/element layouts for validation.

nodes.name: WebGLCommand
nodes.summary: Exhaustive enum of WebGL commands covering the entire GL/GLES API surface sent to the WebGL thread.

nodes.name: WebGLMsg
nodes.summary: Top-level message enum for the WebGL thread handling context creation, resizing, command dispatch, buffer swaps, and shutdown.

nodes.name: WebGLMsgSender
nodes.summary: Handle for sending commands to a specific WebGL context over its channel, with helpers for image keys, resizing, and removal.

nodes.name: WebGLThreads
nodes.summary: Abstraction over the WebGL channel(s) providing pipeline access, exit, and resource cleanup.

nodes.name: WebXRCommand
nodes.summary: Enum of WebXR-specific commands for layer manager and frame lifecycle.

nodes.name: GLLimits
nodes.summary: Struct capturing the WebGL context capability limits queried from the GL driver, exposed to script.

nodes.name: WebGLError
nodes.summary: Enum of WebGL error codes returned to script for invalid operations.

nodes.name: WebGLVersion
nodes.summary: Enum distinguishing WebGL1 versus WebGL2 contexts.

nodes.name: WebGLCreateContextResult
nodes.summary: Result of creating a WebGL context, carrying the sender channel, limits, GLSL version, and API type.

nodes.name: SizedDataType
nodes.summary: Enum of sized GL data types (int8 through float32) used to validate buffer and uniform layouts.

nodes.name: to_unsized
nodes.summary: Maps a sized GL texture/internal format to its unsized equivalent for validation.

nodes.name: compatible_data_types
nodes.summary: Returns the set of data types compatible with a given GL type/format combination for copy and readback validation.

nodes.name: sized_data_type
nodes.summary: Resolves the sized data type for a GL constant, including packed bit-field interpretation for combined formats.

nodes.name: element_size
nodes.summary: Computes the byte size of a single element for a given sized data type and component count.

nodes.name: components_per_element
nodes.summary: Determines the number of components per element for a given GL data type.

nodes.name: required_webgl_version
nodes.summary: Returns the minimum WebGL version required by a given GL constant.

nodes.name: webgl_channel
nodes.summary: Creates a new channel pair for communicating with the WebGL thread.

nodes.name: clear_painter_resources
nodes.summary: Sends a message to release a painter's WebGL resources and waits for confirmation.

nodes.name: encoding.rs
nodes.summary: Provides URL query-string encoding that percent-encodes characters not representable in the target character encoding (e.g. ISO-2022-JP) as HTML numeric character references.

nodes.name: lib.rs
nodes.summary: Defines the `ServoUrl` wrapper type and `UrlError` enum, providing a copy-on-write Arc-backed URL abstraction with parsing, mutation, and scheme/security helpers used throughout Servo.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a newtype over `Arc<Url>` with `Arc::make_mut` for cheap copy-on-write mutation.

nodes.name: origin.rs
nodes.summary: Implements origin types (`ImmutableOrigin`, `MutableOrigin`, `OpaqueOrigin`) with same-origin comparisons, snapshotting for script state, and potentially-trustworthy checks.
nodes.languageNotes: Models the mutable domain via `Rc<RefCell<Option<String>>>` shared between immutable and mutable origins.

nodes.name: encode_as_url_query_string
nodes.summary: Encodes a string into a URL query string under the given character encoding, mapping unmappable characters to HTML numeric character references.

nodes.name: UrlError
nodes.summary: Error enum describing URL mutation failures such as setting a username, IP host, password, or converting to/from a file path.

nodes.name: ServoUrl
nodes.summary: Central URL wrapper type holding an `Arc<Url>`, exposing parsing, accessor, mutation, scheme-classification, and trustworthiness methods over the underlying URL.

nodes.name: debug_compact
nodes.summary: Produces a compact, human-readable debug representation of a URL by stripping scheme and truncating long paths for logging.

nodes.name: is_potentially_trustworthy
nodes.summary: Determines whether a URL should be treated as a potentially trustworthy (secure) context based on scheme and origin.

nodes.name: matches_about_blank
nodes.summary: Checks whether the URL is equivalent to `about:blank`, accounting for empty path, username, password, and host.

nodes.name: ImmutableOrigin
nodes.summary: Immutable origin representation (opaque or scheme/host/port tuple) with constructors, same-origin comparison, and trustworthiness checks.

nodes.name: DomainComparable
nodes.summary: Trait abstracting access to an origin's mutable domain state and immutable form across origin types.

nodes.name: OpaqueOrigin
nodes.summary: Serializable representation of an opaque origin, tracking a unique id and flags for file origins and data-worker origins from secure contexts.

nodes.name: OriginSnapshot
nodes.summary: Snapshot of an origin's immutable state and current domain, used to persist origin state across script contexts.

nodes.name: MutableOrigin
nodes.summary: Mutable origin wrapper allowing the document.domain property to be set while sharing immutable origin state via `Rc<RefCell>`.

nodes.name: is_potentially_trustworthy
nodes.summary: Evaluates whether an origin is a potentially trustworthy context, checking secure schemes, loopback hosts, and trusted domains.

nodes.name: effective_domain
nodes.summary: Returns the origin's effective domain, preferring the explicitly set domain and falling back to the origin host.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with the README to understand what Servo is: a parallel browser engine written in Rust, developed as a research project to explore memory-safe, concurrent rendering. The document gives platform-specific build instructions and sets the context for every component you will visit next — Servo's defining trait is that its major subsystems run as independent threads and processes that talk to each other over typed channels.

tour.title: The Embedder: servoshell Entry Point
tour.description: Servo is an embeddable engine, not a standalone browser, so the actual executable is the 'servoshell' embedder. Its main.rs detaches from the console on Windows and hands off to the embedder main loop, while lib.rs initializes cryptography and tracing and declares the shell's modules. This is the outermost layer: an application that hosts Servo rather than part of Servo itself.

tour.title: The Servo Embedding API
tour.description: Sitting between servoshell and the engine internals, the 'servo' crate is the public embedding API. servo.rs boots the constellation and spins the event loop, webview.rs wraps a single browser view (navigation, input, zoom, screenshots), and servo_delegate.rs defines the ServoDelegate trait through which the engine reports events back to the embedder. This delegate/callback pattern is how Servo stays embedder-agnostic across shells, Android, and OpenHarmony.

tour.title: The Constellation: Multiprocess Brain
tour.description: The constellation is Servo's central coordinator, routing every script and embedder message and managing the lifecycle of content processes. constellation.rs owns navigation, session history, and browsing-context management; pipeline.rs models a single content pipeline with throttling and child pipelines; session_history.rs implements the joint session history used for back/forward navigation. Understanding this actor is key to grasping Servo's multiprocess isolation model.

tour.title: IPC Message Types: The Shared Contract
tour.description: Because Servo's components live in separate threads and processes, they communicate only through serialized messages. shared/constellation/lib.rs defines EmbedderToConstellationMessage (navigation, input events, session-history traversal), while shared/embedder/lib.rs defines the geometry, permission, and media-session types flowing back to the embedder. These shared crates are the 'wire protocol' that keeps script, layout, and the compositor decoupled.
tour.languageLesson: Servo uses a Rust message-passing (actor) model: each subsystem is a thread or process receiving typed enums over channels. Message enums are serialized with serde for cross-process IPC, so adding a feature means extending the enum and its handler — the compiler then flags every unhandled case.

tour.title: The Script Component & DOM
tour.description: The script component owns the JavaScript runtime and the entire DOM implementation. script/lib.rs organizes the crate's submodules, dom/mod.rs is the barrel declaring every DOM subsystem, and node/mod.rs re-exports the thirteen node submodules that implement the core Node interface. This is the largest and most web-standards-heavy part of Servo, where each DOM interface maps to a Rust struct.

tour.title: WebIDL Bindings: Rust to JavaScript
tour.description: Servo does not hand-write the glue between Rust DOM structs and SpiderMonkey JavaScript. script_bindings/lib.rs is the crate root, codegen.py is a Python generator that parses WebIDL files and emits Rust classes, proxy handlers, and unions at build time, and reflector.rs implements the Reflector that binds each Rust DOM struct to its JS object and tracks its memory. This codegen layer is the backbone of Servo's DOM performance.
tour.languageLesson: Servo generates its bindings rather than writing them: a build.rs invokes a Python codegen tool that reads .webidl interface descriptions and emits Rust. The #[dom_struct] procedural macro (components/dom_struct) marks DOM structs so the generator and the JS rooting/tracing system can treat them specially — a hallmark of Rust-based browser engineering.

tour.title: The Layout Engine
tour.description: Layout turns a DOM tree plus computed styles into a box/fragment tree and display list. layout/lib.rs defines the ConstraintSpace and ContainingBlock enums that drive the new layout system; traversal.rs performs incremental traversal, rebuilding only damaged portions of the box tree; and construct_modern.rs builds block containers and anonymous boxes. The shared/layout crate exposes the Layout service and reflow messages used by the script thread.

tour.title: Networking & URL Handling
tour.description: The net component performs resource loading for the browser. net/lib.rs is the crate root, while shared/net/lib.rs exposes the FetchThread and ResourceThread APIs along with cookies, TLS state, and network errors. ServoUrl in url/lib.rs is the copy-on-write Arc-backed URL type used everywhere, wrapping parsing and scheme/security helpers. This layer feeds every fetch, image, and script load from the DOM back to the renderer.

tour.title: Foundation, Config & Procedural Macros
tour.description: Beneath the domain-specific components sit the shared foundations. shared/base/lib.rs re-exports foundational utilities like epoch types and the IPC send trait; config/lib.rs provides command-line parsing and preference management; and dom_struct/lib.rs defines the #[dom_struct] attribute macro that powers the DOM's rooting discipline. These crates are the common substrate every other component builds on.

tour.title: Build, Toolchain & CI
tour.description: Servo is a large Cargo workspace pinned to a specific Rust toolchain. The root Cargo.toml defines shared metadata, dependency versions, lint config, and multiple build profiles (dev, production, coverage, profiling), while rust-toolchain.toml pins the compiler channel and target components. The main.yml GitHub Actions workflow ties it together, orchestrating the builds and tests that keep the many platform backends green.
tour.languageLesson: A Cargo workspace lets many related crates share one Cargo.lock and inherit workspace-level lint and dependency settings. rust-toolchain.toml makes the build reproducible by pinning the exact compiler, and CI matrices run the same workspace across Linux, macOS, and Windows.
